topics.title: Internet Standards
topics.definition: Internet standards are agreed specifications that let different systems and vendors work together.

children.title: RFC documents and IETF
children.definition: Requests for comments are the working documents of the Internet Engineering Task Force, and some become full standards after maturity levels.

children.title: W3C, ISO and IEEE
children.definition: W3C standardises web technologies, ISO standardises broad information technology and IEEE standardises local area networks.

children.title: Maturity levels of a standard
children.definition: Proposed standard, draft standard, Internet standard and historic or experimental status.

children.title: Why standards matter
children.definition: Interoperability, portability and the ability of any browser to talk to any server.

topics.title: Introduction to the World Wide Web
topics.definition: The web is an information system of linked hypertext documents accessed over the Internet.

children.title: Web page, website and hyperlinks
children.definition: A page is one document, a site is a collection of related pages and hyperlinks connect them.

children.title: Web browser and web server
children.definition: The browser requests and renders content while the server stores and delivers it.

children.title: Static versus dynamic pages
children.definition: Static pages are stored ready made, dynamic pages are generated for each request.

children.title: Web evolution: Web 1.0 to Web 3.0
children.definition: From read only pages to social and interactive applications to semantic and decentralised ideas.

topics.title: WWW Architecture
topics.definition: WWW architecture describes how browsers, servers and the network cooperate to deliver web content.

children.title: Client server model of the web
children.definition: The browser is the client, the web server is the server and HTTP carries the requests and responses.

children.title: Three tier architecture
children.definition: Presentation, application logic and data tiers separate the interface, business rules and storage.

children.title: Web server software and hosting
children.definition: Apache, Nginx and IIS serve content from a document root with configuration for virtual hosts.

children.title: Web caching and proxies
children.definition: Forward and reverse proxies plus content delivery networks reduce latency and server load.

topics.title: SMTP, POP3 and IMAP
topics.definition: Email is delivered by push protocols and retrieved by pull protocols.

children.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)
children.definition: Push protocol on port 25 that sends mail from client to server and between servers.

children.title: Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP3)
children.definition: Pull protocol on port 110 that downloads messages, usually deleting them from the server.

children.title: Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)
children.definition: Port 143 protocol that keeps mail on the server, supports folders and synchronises across devices.

children.title: Email message format and MIME
children.definition: Headers plus body defined by RFC 822, with MIME allowing attachments and non-ASCII content.

topics.title: File Transfer Protocol (FTP)
topics.definition: FTP transfers files between a client and a server using two separate connections.

children.title: Control and data connections
children.definition: The control connection on port 21 carries commands while the data connection carries the file.

children.title: Active and passive modes
children.definition: Active lets the server open the data connection to the client; passive lets the client open it, which works through firewalls.

children.title: FTP commands and replies
children.definition: USER, PASS, RETR, STOR, LIST and QUIT with three digit reply codes.

children.title: Secure alternatives
children.definition: SFTP over SSH and FTPS over TLS replace plain FTP for confidential transfers.

topics.title: Overview of HTTP and the Request Response Model
topics.definition: HTTP is the stateless request response protocol of the web.

children.title: Request message structure
children.definition: Request line with method and URL, headers, a blank line and an optional body.

children.title: Response message structure
children.definition: Status line, headers such as content type and length, a blank line and the body.

children.title: Methods and status codes
children.definition: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD and OPTIONS; 1xx to 5xx status classes.

children.title: Headers, content types and cookies
children.definition: Metadata such as Accept, User-Agent and Set-Cookie that shape caching, sessions and content negotiation.

children.title: Persistent connections and pipelining
children.definition: Keep alive lets many requests share one TCP connection, which lowers latency.

children.title: HTTPS
children.definition: HTTP over TLS encrypts traffic and verifies the server identity with certificates.

topics.title: Generation of Dynamic Web Pages
topics.definition: Dynamic pages are built at request time on the server, on the client or on both.

children.title: Common Gateway Interface (CGI)
children.definition: An old standard in which the server starts a separate program for each request, which is simple but slow.

children.title: Server side scripting
children.definition: PHP, JSP, ASP.NET, Python and Node.js generate HTML on the server before it is sent.

children.title: Client side scripting
children.definition: JavaScript runs in the browser to update the page without a full reload.

children.title: Server side includes and templating
children.definition: Reusable fragments and templates are combined with data to build the final page.

modules.title: HTML and CSS for User Interface Design

topics.title: Introduction to HTML and HTML5
topics.definition: HTML is the markup language that gives structure and meaning to web content.

children.title: Document structure
children.definition: DOCTYPE, html, head with title and meta tags, and body holding the visible content.

children.title: Tags, elements and attributes
children.definition: Elements are written with opening and closing tags and configured by attributes such as id, class and src.

children.title: HTML5 semantic elements
children.definition: header, nav, main, section, article, aside, figure and footer describe the role of each part.

children.title: HTML5 features
children.definition: Native audio and video, canvas, SVG, local storage, web workers and better form input types.

children.title: Headings and paragraph elements
children.definition: h1 to h6 for hierarchy and p, br and hr for text blocks and breaks.

topics.title: Formatting, Fonts, Comments and Backgrounds
topics.definition: Formatting elements control the look of text while comments document the code.

children.title: Text formatting elements
children.definition: b, i, u, strong, em, sub, sup, mark, small and del change the appearance or meaning of text.

children.title: Fonts and colours
children.definition: The font tag is obsolete; modern pages use CSS font-family, size and colour instead.

children.title: Commenting code
children.definition: Comments are written between the symbols for less-than, exclamation, two dashes and their mirror image, and are ignored by the browser.

children.title: Backgrounds
children.definition: Background colour and images were set with attributes in old HTML and are set with CSS today.

topics.title: Anchors, Hyperlinks and Images
topics.definition: Links connect documents and images embed pictures in a page.

children.title: Anchor tag and href
children.definition: The a element creates a link using href, which may point to a page, a section, an email address or a file.

children.title: Types of hyperlinks
children.definition: Internal links within a site, external links to other sites, and fragment links to a section of the same page.

children.title: Target attribute and link behaviour
children.definition: target makes a link open in a new tab or a named frame.

children.title: Image tag, alt text and formats
children.definition: The img element uses src and alt with JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG and WebP formats for different needs.

children.title: Image maps and figure captions
children.definition: Map regions of one image to different links and use figure with figcaption for captions.

topics.title: Lists, Tables and Frames
topics.definition: Lists group items, tables arrange data in rows and columns and frames embed or split content.

children.title: Ordered and unordered lists
children.definition: ol numbers items and ul marks them with bullets, with li marking each item and nested lists allowed.

children.title: Definition lists
children.definition: dl with dt for the term and dd for its description.

children.title: Creating tables
children.definition: table, caption, thead, tbody, tr, th and td give rows, headers and cells.

children.title: Rowspan and colspan plus nested tables
children.definition: Cells can span several rows or columns, and tables can be nested inside cells.

children.title: Framesets and iframes
children.definition: Framesets split a window into panes and are obsolete; iframe embeds another document inside a page.

topics.title: HTML Forms
topics.definition: Forms collect user input and submit it to a server for processing.

children.title: Form element and action
children.definition: The form tag names the processing URL with action and the sending method with method, usually GET or POST.

children.title: Input types
children.definition: text, password, email, number, date, radio, checkbox, file, hidden, submit and reset with attributes name, value and placeholder.

children.title: Select, option, textarea and button
children.definition: Drop down lists, multi-line text and buttons with caption or image.

children.title: Labels, fieldsets and accessibility
children.definition: label ties text to a control and fieldset with legend groups related controls.

children.title: Client side validation attributes
children.definition: required, pattern, min, max and maxlength check input before submission, with HTML5 validation messages.

topics.title: Cascading Style Sheets: Need, Syntax and Types
topics.definition: CSS separates presentation from content and controls layout, colour and typography.

children.title: Why CSS is needed
children.definition: Consistency across pages, easier maintenance, smaller HTML and separation of concerns.

children.title: Syntax and structure
children.definition: A rule has a selector and a declaration block of property value pairs, with comments and units.

children.title: Inline styles
children.definition: Applied with the style attribute on one element only, which has the highest priority but cannot be reused.

children.title: Embedded (internal) style sheets
children.definition: Written in a style element in the head, which applies to one page.

children.title: Linking external style sheets
children.definition: The link element with rel stylesheet shares one CSS file across an entire site.

children.title: Cascade, specificity and inheritance
children.definition: Later, more specific rules win, and inheritable properties pass from parent to child.

topics.title: CSS Text, Backgrounds, Box Model and Positioning
topics.definition: CSS controls typography, colour, spacing and where each element appears.

children.title: Text manipulation
children.definition: font-family, font-size, font-weight, line-height, letter-spacing, text-align and text-decoration.

children.title: Backgrounds and borders
children.definition: Background colour, gradients or images, with border radius and box shadow for styling.

children.title: Margins and padding
children.definition: Margin is space outside the border and padding is space inside it; the box model is content, padding, border and margin.

children.title: Width, height and overflow
children.definition: Box sizing decides whether padding is included in the width, and overflow decides what happens to excess content.

children.title: Positioning
children.definition: Static, relative, absolute, fixed and sticky positioning, with z-index for stacking order.

children.title: Float, flexbox and grid
children.definition: Floats for wrapping text, flexbox for one dimensional layouts and grid for two dimensional layouts.

children.title: Responsive design and media queries
children.definition: Percentages, flexible units and media queries adapt one layout to phones, tablets and desktops.

topics.title: JavaScript: Introduction and Core Features
topics.definition: JavaScript is the scripting language of the browser that makes pages interactive and can also run on servers.

children.title: Where JavaScript runs
children.definition: In the browser engine, inside HTML with the script tag, in external files and on the server through Node.js.

children.title: Core features
children.definition: Interpreted, dynamically typed, object based, event driven and single threaded with an event loop.

children.title: Advantages and limitations
children.definition: Fast client side validation and rich interfaces, but browser differences and client side security limits.

children.title: Adding JavaScript to a page
children.definition: Inline handlers, the script element inside head or body, and external .js files with defer or async.

topics.title: Data Types, Variables, Operators and Statements
topics.definition: JavaScript variables hold values of primitive or object types, and expressions are built with operators and statements.

children.title: Data types
children.definition: Primitive types string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, null and symbol, plus object types including arrays and functions.

children.title: Variables: var, let and const
children.definition: var is function scoped and hoisted, let is block scoped and const cannot be reassigned.

children.title: Operators and expressions
children.definition: Arithmetic, comparison with == and ===, logical, assignment, ternary and typeof operators.

children.title: Statements and control flow
children.definition: if, else, switch, for, while, do while, for of, for in, break, continue and try catch finally.

children.title: Type conversion and coercion
children.definition: Implicit conversion by operators and explicit conversion with Number, String and Boolean.

topics.title: Functions
topics.definition: A function is a reusable block of code that may take parameters and return a value.

children.title: Function declaration and expression
children.definition: Declarations are hoisted while function expressions are assigned to variables.

children.title: Parameters, arguments and return
children.definition: Parameters receive values, arguments holds them, and return sends a value back with undefined as the default.

children.title: Scope, closures and hoisting
children.definition: A closure remembers the variables of the function that created it.

children.title: Arrow functions and callbacks
children.definition: Shorter syntax with lexical this, commonly used as callbacks and event handlers.

children.title: Rest, spread and default parameters
children.definition: Modern syntax for flexible argument lists and copying or expanding arrays and objects.

topics.title: Objects, Arrays, Date and Math
topics.definition: JavaScript provides built-in objects for structured data, dates and mathematical operations.

children.title: Objects and properties
children.definition: Objects store key value pairs; properties and methods are accessed with a dot or brackets.

children.title: Arrays and their methods
children.definition: Arrays are ordered collections with push, pop, shift, unshift, slice, splice, map, filter, reduce, sort and forEach.

children.title: Strings and their methods
children.definition: length, charAt, indexOf, substring, slice, split, replace, toUpperCase and trim.

children.title: Date object
children.definition: Creates and manipulates dates with getFullYear, getMonth, getTime and parsing of date strings.

children.title: Math object
children.definition: Math.round, floor, ceil, abs, pow, sqrt, random, min and max.

children.title: Regular expressions
children.definition: Patterns used with test, match, replace and split for validation and searching.

topics.title: Document Object Model (DOM)
topics.definition: The DOM is a tree representation of the page that JavaScript can read and modify.

children.title: DOM tree and nodes
children.definition: Elements, attributes and text form a hierarchy under the document node.

children.title: Selecting elements
children.definition: getElementById, getElementsByClassName, getElementsByTagName, querySelector and querySelectorAll.

children.title: Changing content and attributes
children.definition: innerHTML, textContent, setAttribute, classList, and style manipulation.

children.title: Creating and removing elements
children.definition: createElement, appendChild, insertBefore, removeChild and cloneNode for dynamic page updates.

children.title: Traversing the DOM
children.definition: parentNode, children, firstElementChild, nextElementSibling and closest.

topics.title: Event Handling
topics.definition: Event handling lets the page respond to user actions such as clicks, typing and scrolling.

children.title: Event and event object
children.definition: The event object carries the type, target, coordinates, key and modifiers.

children.title: Event handlers and listeners
children.definition: Inline handlers, properties such as onclick and addEventListener with options.

children.title: Event flow: capture, target and bubble
children.definition: Events travel down to the target and bubble back up, and stopPropagation stops the journey.

children.title: Event delegation
children.definition: One listener on a parent handles events from many children, which is efficient for lists.

children.title: Common events
children.definition: click, dblclick, mouseover, keydown, keyup, change, input, submit, load, scroll and touch events.

children.title: Form events and validation
children.definition: preventDefault is used to stop submission while custom validation runs.

topics.title: Controlling Windows, Frames and Documents
topics.definition: JavaScript can open, resize, move and close windows and can access frames and documents.

children.title: Window object
children.definition: open, close, alert, confirm, prompt, moveTo, resizeTo, setTimeout and setInterval.

children.title: Navigator, screen, history and location
children.definition: Browser information, display size, browsing history and the current URL, with location.href performing redirection.

children.title: Frames and iframes
children.definition: Frame collections and accessing the document of a same origin frame.

children.title: Timers and animation
children.definition: setTimeout and setInterval drive repeated updates and simple animations.

topics.title: Form Handling and Validation in JavaScript
topics.definition: Forms are validated in the browser before submission to save server work and give instant feedback.

children.title: Accessing form elements
children.definition: document.forms, element names and values, checkbox and radio checked states.

children.title: Validation techniques
children.definition: Checking empty fields, lengths, patterns with regular expressions and numeric ranges.

children.title: Validation events and error display
children.definition: onsubmit, onblur and oninput with error messages placed near fields.

children.title: Advantages and limits of client side validation
children.definition: Fast feedback, but it can be bypassed, so server side validation is still required.

topics.title: Browser and Media Management
topics.definition: Browsers expose objects that let scripts manage windows, navigation and media content.

children.title: Browser object model
children.definition: window, document, navigator, screen, history and location together form the BOM.

children.title: Cookies and web storage
children.definition: Cookies carry small data with every request while localStorage and sessionStorage keep data in the browser only.

children.title: Handling images, audio and video
children.definition: The image objects, audio and video elements with play, pause, currentTime and volume control.

children.title: Canvas and SVG
children.definition: Canvas draws pixels through the 2D context while SVG describes vector graphics as XML.

children.title: Geolocation and device APIs
children.definition: The geolocation API, drag and drop, and the file reader API extend browser behaviour.

topics.title: Classes, Constructors and Object Orientation in JavaScript
topics.definition: Modern JavaScript provides class syntax over a prototype based object model.

children.title: Object constructors
children.definition: A constructor function initialises objects with this and new, and methods are placed on the prototype.

children.title: Prototypes and the prototype chain
children.definition: Objects inherit properties through links up the chain to Object.prototype.

children.title: Encapsulation with closures and private fields
children.definition: Data privacy is achieved with closures or the hash prefix private fields and static members.

children.title: ES6 class syntax
children.definition: class with constructor, methods, getters and setters is syntactic sugar over prototypes.

children.title: Inheritance: subclasses and superclasses
children.definition: extends creates a subclass and super calls the parent constructor or method.

children.title: Polymorphism and method overriding
children.definition: A subclass may replace a parent method, and the most derived version is called.

topics.title: JSON
topics.definition: JavaScript Object Notation is a text format for exchanging structured data between a browser and a server.

children.title: JSON syntax rules
children.definition: Objects with quoted keys, arrays, strings, numbers, true, false and null, with no functions or comments.

children.title: JSON.parse and JSON.stringify
children.definition: Converting between a JSON string and a JavaScript object in both directions.

children.title: JSON versus XML
children.definition: JSON is lighter, easier to parse and native to JavaScript, while XML supports schemas, attributes and namespaces.

children.title: JSON in web APIs
children.definition: REST services send and receive JSON, which is the standard format of modern web APIs.

topics.title: jQuery
topics.definition: jQuery is a small JavaScript library that simplifies DOM traversal, events, animation and AJAX.

children.title: Selectors and chaining
children.definition: The jQuery function selects elements with CSS style selectors and methods can be chained.

children.title: DOM manipulation and effects
children.definition: text, html, attr, addClass, append, remove, show, hide, fadeIn and slideToggle.

children.title: Events in jQuery
children.definition: on, click, hover and ready centralise event handling with the shorthand dollar ready function.

children.title: AJAX helpers
children.definition: get, post and ajax methods wrap XMLHttpRequest for short code.

children.title: Advantages and disadvantages
children.definition: Cross browser convenience and a large plugin base versus extra download size and reduced need today.

topics.title: AJAX
topics.definition: AJAX updates part of a page by exchanging data with the server in the background without reloading the page.

children.title: How AJAX works
children.definition: JavaScript sends an asynchronous request, the server replies with data, and the DOM is updated from the response.

children.title: XMLHttpRequest steps
children.definition: Create the object, open the request, set the callback, send it, then read readyState and status in the handler.

children.title: The fetch API and promises
children.definition: fetch returns a promise with json and text methods, used with async and await for cleaner code.

children.title: Same origin policy and CORS
children.definition: Cross origin requests are blocked unless the server allows them with CORS headers.

children.title: Advantages and issues
children.definition: Smoother interfaces and less data transfer, but bookmarking, history and search engine indexing become harder.

topics.title: How the Web Works with PHP and the LAMP Stack
topics.definition: PHP is a server side scripting language that runs on the web server and outputs HTML.

children.title: Request response with PHP
children.definition: The browser requests a .php page, the server executes the script and returns the generated HTML.

children.title: Setting up the environment with LAMP
children.definition: Linux, Apache, MySQL and PHP form the classic free hosting stack, with XAMPP or WAMP for local practice.

children.title: PHP versus client side scripting
children.definition: PHP code runs on the server and the user never sees it, while JavaScript runs in the browser and is visible.

children.title: PHP file structure
children.definition: PHP code is written inside the opening and closing PHP tags and can be mixed with HTML.

topics.title: PHP Basics: Syntax, Variables and Constants
topics.definition: PHP scripts use loosely typed variables with a dollar sign and constants defined once.

children.title: Basic syntax and statements
children.definition: Statements end with a semicolon, comments use double slash, hash or block syntax, and case matters for variables.

children.title: Variables and scope
children.definition: Variables start with $, are dynamically typed, and have local, global and static scope with superglobals such as GET and POST.

children.title: Constants
children.definition: define and const create values that cannot change, and predefined constants include PHP_VERSION and __FILE__.

children.title: Data types and type juggling
children.definition: String, integer, float, boolean, array, object, null and resource, with automatic conversion in expressions.

topics.title: Print and Echo
topics.definition: PHP outputs content to the browser with echo, print, print_r and var_dump.

children.title: echo and print
children.definition: echo can take several arguments and is slightly faster, while print returns a value and takes one argument.

children.title: print_r and var_dump
children.definition: Debugging helpers that display arrays and objects in readable form.

children.title: printf and number formatting
children.definition: Formatted output with placeholders such as percent s, percent d and percent f.

children.title: Embedding output in HTML
children.definition: Short echo tags and heredoc syntax mix dynamic values into markup.

topics.title: Strings and Arrays in PHP
topics.definition: PHP offers many string functions and three kinds of arrays.

children.title: String functions
children.definition: strlen, strpos, substr, str_replace, strtoupper, trim, explode, implode and nl2br.

children.title: String interpolation
children.definition: Double quoted strings expand variables while single quoted strings do not.

children.title: Indexed arrays
children.definition: Arrays with numeric keys accessed by position, created with array or square brackets.

children.title: Associative arrays
children.definition: Arrays with named keys, used like records with field names.

children.title: Multidimensional arrays
children.definition: Arrays of arrays used for tables and grouped data.

children.title: Array functions
children.definition: count, sort, ksort, array_push, array_pop, array_merge, array_keys, array_values and foreach traversal.

topics.title: Operators, Control Structures and Functions in PHP
topics.definition: PHP supports the usual operators, branches, loops and user defined functions.

children.title: Operators
children.definition: Arithmetic, assignment, comparison with == and ===, logical, increment, string concatenation with a dot and the null coalescing operator.

children.title: Conditional statements
children.definition: if, else, elseif, switch and the match expression.

children.title: Loops
children.definition: for, while, do while and foreach, with break and continue.

children.title: User defined functions
children.definition: Declared with the function keyword, with parameters, default values, variadic arguments, type hints and return values.

children.title: Include and require
children.definition: include and require reuse code from other files, with require stopping the script on failure.

children.title: Superglobals and sessions
children.definition: GET, POST, REQUEST, SERVER, COOKIE and SESSION carry data between requests.

topics.title: Reading Data in Web Pages
topics.definition: PHP reads user input from forms, URLs and cookies to build dynamic responses.

children.title: GET versus POST
children.definition: GET places data in the URL, is visible and limited in size; POST sends it in the request body and is safer for sensitive data.

children.title: Handling form input
children.definition: Reading the name attributes through the POST superglobal and validating each field on the server.

children.title: Validation and sanitisation
children.definition: filter_var, htmlspecialchars and trim defend against bad input, SQL injection and cross site scripting.

children.title: Uploading files
children.definition: The FILES superglobal with move_uploaded_file stores uploaded files after checking type and size.

children.title: Cookies and sessions
children.definition: setcookie stores small data on the client while session_start keeps server side state with a session id.

topics.title: Connecting PHP with MySQL
topics.definition: PHP connects to MySQL to store and retrieve application data with SQL statements.

children.title: Creating a connection
children.definition: mysqli_connect or new PDO with host, user, password and database name, plus error handling.

children.title: Executing queries
children.definition: mysqli_query or prepared statements run SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements.

children.title: Fetching results
children.definition: Associative and numeric fetch modes, mysqli_fetch_assoc, fetch_all and loops that print rows into a table.

children.title: Prepared statements
children.definition: Parameterised queries with bind_param or PDO bindValue prevent SQL injection.

children.title: Insert, update and delete with feedback
children.definition: Affected rows and insert id confirm the result of a data change.

children.title: Closing connections and error handling
children.definition: Frees results and closes the connection, with try catch or mysqli error checks for failures.

children.title: A small complete example
children.definition: A student form that inserts a record and lists all students joins HTML forms, PHP and MySQL end to end.
